canonical_statement: The report describes a travel-associated case of non-toxigenic, penicillin-resistant cutaneous Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection in a previously healthy 14-year-old girl.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we report a case of non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae in a previously healthy 14-year-old girl

canonical_statement: The patient was a 14-year-old girl with no significant past medical history.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 14-year-old girl with no significant past medical history

canonical_statement: The patient was born in Ethiopia, had lived in the United Kingdom since early childhood, and her diphtheria vaccinations were reported as up to date.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The patient was born in Ethiopia and had lived in the UK since she was a young child. Her vaccinations were up-to-date.

population.label: Vaccinated adolescent living in the United Kingdom

canonical_statement: The patient returned from a one-month stay in Ethiopia the day before presentation and had cut her right lower leg on a rusty metal gate about three weeks earlier.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The day prior to her presentation, she returned from a one-month stay with relatives in Ethiopia.

concept.text: Recent travel to Ethiopia and traumatic leg wound

exposures.details: One-month stay; rusty metal gate injury about three weeks before presentation

canonical_statement: She presented with several bilateral ulcerated lesions on the lower legs and soles with foul-smelling discharge, and she was afebrile and not systemically ill.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: presented with several bilateral ulcerated skin lesions on her lower legs and the soles of feet

canonical_statement: Initial inpatient antimicrobial therapy consisted of intravenous benzylpenicillin and intravenous flucloxacillin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The patient was initially prescribed IV benzylpenicillin and IV flucloxacillin.

canonical_statement: The work-up included a malaria film, stool and wound cultures, and targeted inoculation of skin swabs onto Hoyle agar when cutaneous diphtheria entered the differential diagnosis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A request was made for her skin swabs to be put onto Hoyle's agar to determine if C. diphtheriae was present.

canonical_statement: Group A Streptococcus was isolated from the skin swabs; after flucloxacillin was replaced with benzylpenicillin, the cellulitis did not improve as expected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Group A Streptococcus was isolated from her skin swabs.

canonical_statement: Black colonies on Hoyle agar were Gram-positive bacilli, and the reference laboratory used PCR and ELEK testing to characterize the isolate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The reference laboratory confirmed that the bacteria were non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae via PCR and ELEK testing.

canonical_statement: The reference laboratory confirmed non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: confirmed that the bacteria were non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae via PCR and ELEK testing

canonical_statement: The article reports the Corynebacterium diphtheriae isolate as penicillin resistant and erythromycin sensitive.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is the first clinical case of penicillin-resistant C. diphtheriae in the UK.

canonical_statement: Oral erythromycin was added after the Corynebacterium diphtheriae result.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PO erythromycin was added to the treatment.

canonical_statement: Erythromycin caused nausea and vomiting and was replaced by oral azithromycin after one day.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Erythromycin caused nausea and vomiting and was therefore replaced with PO azithromycin after 1 day.

canonical_statement: After three days of macrolide therapy, benzylpenicillin was stopped and four additional days of oral azithromycin were planned to complete one week of macrolide treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a further four days of PO azithromycin such that she would receive one total week of macrolide treatment

exposures.duration: four additional days; one week total macrolide treatment

exposures.details: stopped after three days of macrolide therapy

canonical_statement: The ulcerations were described as notably improved when the patient was discharged.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Her ulcerations exhibited notably improvement, and she was allowed go home at this point.

canonical_statement: Public health and hospital infection-control teams were notified; the patient was isolated while diphtheria was suspected, and family screening occurred before the strain was known to be non-toxigenic.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Public health had screened her family prior to being informed that the bacteria were a non-toxigenic strain.

canonical_statement: The authors considered penicillin resistance clinically important because penicillin was the first-line recommended empiric option for suspected diphtheria in nonallergic patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: penicillin is the first-line recommended choice for empiric therapy for patients who are suspected of having Diphtheria

canonical_statement: The authors recommended considering non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria in the differential diagnosis of fully vaccinated patients with cutaneous ulcers and recent foreign travel.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: non-toxigenic cutaneous Diphtheria should be considered among the differentials

canonical_statement: The authors stated that this was the first reported clinical case of penicillin-resistant Corynebacterium diphtheriae in the United Kingdom.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To our knowledge, this is the first report of a clinical case of penicillin-resistant C. diphtheriae in the UK.

canonical_statement: In its narrative review, the article reports five Brazilian cases of infective endocarditis due to non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae, with four cases in females aged 7-14 years and 40% mortality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Over the past 10 years, five cases of infectious endocarditis due to non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae have been reported in Brazil.

canonical_statement: The article reports a Vancouver series of 37 non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria cases over 10 years; among 33 reviewed charts, 31 cases occurred among the urban poor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In Vancouver, 37 cases of non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria were reported in the 10-year period ending in 2007.

canonical_statement: The article reports 25 non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae cases in Poland from 2004-2012, of which 18 were invasive, and states that 17% had no concomitant disease or identified risk factors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Of 25 cases of non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae observed in Poland between 2004 and 2012, 18 were invasive.

canonical_statement: The article summarizes a Polish case of bacteremia and infective endocarditis due to non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae in a 38-year-old man whose reported comorbidity was cigarette smoking.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 38-year-old male whose only comorbidity was smoking 20 cigarettes per day developed bacteremia and infectious endocarditis

canonical_statement: The article summarizes a case of bacteremia due to non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae in a 23-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 23-year-old male with AML developed bacteremia of unknown origin from a nontoxigenic strain of C. diphtheriae.

canonical_statement: The article summarizes prosthetic mitral-valve endocarditis due to non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae in a 54-year-old woman.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 54-year-old female with a prosthetic mitral valve was reported to have developed prosthetic mitral valve endocarditis
